title: Drishyam 3 Ends BookMyShow Run As Bollywood's Tenth Highest Ticket-Seller Ever
excerpt: The Hindi crime thriller starring Ajay Devgn sold 6.72 million tickets on BookMyShow in five weeks and closed with 379.65 crore net in India, becoming Devgn's highest ticket-selling film on the platform.
body:
• Drishyam 3 sold 6.72 million tickets on BookMyShow in its five-week run, the highest for a Bollywood crime thriller on the platform.
  • It finished as Bollywood's tenth-highest ticket-selling film ever on BookMyShow, passing Mahavatar Narsimha's 6.61 million.
  • The Hindi film closed its run with 379.65 crore net in India after a 62 crore opening, according to Koimoi and Zoom TV.
  • Directed by Abhishek Pathak, it is Ajay Devgn's highest ticket-selling film on BookMyShow since per-hour trending was introduced.

Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 has ended its BookMyShow run as Bollywood's tenth-highest ticket-selling film ever on the platform, closing a five-week theatrical run that made it the star's biggest grosser even though it fell short of the 400- to 500-crore net figures some had expected.

The Hindi-language crime thriller — officially Drishyam: The Conclusion, directed by Abhishek Pathak — sold a total of 6.72 million tickets on BookMyShow, Koimoi reported. Zoom TV reported the same 6.72 million figure and the same tenth-place finish.

The numbers behind the ranking

On BookMyShow, 6.72 million tickets is the highest number for a Bollywood crime thriller since per-hour trending was introduced for ticket sales, according to both reports. It is also Ajay Devgn's highest ticket-selling movie on the platform in that period.

Among all Bollywood films, Drishyam 3 passed Mahavatar Narsimha, which sold 6.61 million tickets, to claim tenth place. Koimoi's all-time BookMyShow list is led by Dhurandhar 2 at 18.37 million, followed by Dhurandhar at 14.19 million, Chhaava at 12.59 million, Jawan at 12.4 million and Stree 2 at 11.16 million, with Animal, Gadar 2, Hanuman Ansh and Saiyaara also ahead of Drishyam 3.

That gap matters for how the result should be read: Drishyam 3 did not rival the very biggest event films on ticket volume, but a dialogue-driven thriller reaching the all-time top ten on tickets — not just on rupee collections helped by premium pricing — points to broad footfalls rather than a narrow, high-price opening.

A strong close, short of the loftiest forecasts

Domestically, the film opened with 62 crore net and finished its fifth week with a total of 379.65 crore net, Koimoi and Zoom TV reported. Koimoi noted it was not as leggy a run as its predecessor, Drishyam 2, but still emerged as Ajay Devgn's top grosser.

With Ramayana now in release, Koimoi said the film has almost ended its run and will not earn significantly in its remaining days, and that it will no longer appear in BookMyShow's per-hour trending — the platform marker that its BookMyShow run has officially wrapped up.

The film

Drishyam 3 is a Hindi film, a point confirmed by its listing as a 2026 Indian Hindi-language crime thriller. It is directed by Abhishek Pathak and produced by Kumar Mangat Pathak, Abhishek Pathak, Ajit Andhare and Alok Jain under Panorama Studios and Star Studio18.

Alongside Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar, the cast includes Jaideep Ahlawat, Tabu, Rajat Kapoor, Kamlesh Sawant, Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav and Prakash Raj, according to Koimoi.

For diaspora audiences, who tracked the franchise through its earlier chapters and watched this concluding Hindi installment in North American theatres as well, the BookMyShow ranking is an India-side measure only — it counts tickets sold on that platform in India, not overseas collections. Even on that narrower measure, a crime thriller with no large-scale action spectacle finishing in Bollywood's all-time top ten for tickets is the story: the Salgaonkar saga ended as a genuine crowd-puller, not only a critical talking point.
